classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish horizontal and vertical dilations and coordinate three related exponential or logarithmic curves on each set of axes.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Use dilations to sketch these graphs on the one set of axes:
$$y=3^x\qquad y=2\times3^x\qquad y=3^{2x}$$

answer.short: $y=2\times3^x$ is a vertical dilation of $y=3^x$ by factor $2$; $y=3^{2x}$ is a horizontal dilation by factor $\tfrac12$. All three have asymptote $y=0$.
answer.worked:
Sketch $y=3^x$ through $(-1,\tfrac13)$, $(0,1)$ and $(1,3)$.

For $y=2\times3^x$, double each ordinate: $(x,y)\mapsto(x,2y)$. The corresponding points are $(-1,\tfrac23)$, $(0,2)$ and $(1,6)$.

For $y=3^{2x}$, halve each abscissa: $(x,y)\mapsto(\tfrac{x}{2},y)$. The corresponding points are $(-\tfrac12,\tfrac13)$, $(0,1)$ and $(\tfrac12,3)$. All curves increase and approach the horizontal asymptote $y=0$ to the left.

spec.description: Three equation-driven increasing exponential curves on shared axes; separate line-style legend identifies each curve.
spec.mathematics: Vertical factor 2 and horizontal factor 1/2 applied to y=3^x; common horizontal asymptote y=0.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Use dilations to sketch these graphs on the one set of axes:
$$y=\log_3 x\qquad y=2\log_3 x\qquad y=\log_3 2x$$

answer.short: $y=2\log_3 x$ is a vertical dilation of $y=\log_3 x$ by factor $2$; $y=\log_3(2x)$ is a horizontal dilation by factor $\tfrac12$. Their $x$-intercepts are $1$, $1$ and $\tfrac12$, respectively. All have asymptote $x=0$.
answer.worked:
Sketch $y=\log_3 x$ through $(\tfrac13,-1)$, $(1,0)$ and $(3,1)$.

For $y=2\log_3 x$, double each ordinate: $(x,y)\mapsto(x,2y)$. The corresponding points are $(\tfrac13,-2)$, $(1,0)$ and $(3,2)$.

For $y=\log_3(2x)$, halve each abscissa: $(x,y)\mapsto(\tfrac{x}{2},y)$. The corresponding points are $(\tfrac16,-1)$, $(\tfrac12,0)$ and $(\tfrac32,1)$. All three curves increase for $x>0$ and approach the vertical asymptote $x=0$.

spec.description: Three equation-driven logarithmic curves on shared axes with a separate line-style legend.
spec.mathematics: Vertical factor 2 and horizontal factor 1/2 applied to y=log_3(x); common vertical asymptote x=0.
